title: Test any number
invitation: An open bench for the divisibility activities above: type any whole number, up to 80 digits, and see exactly why it does or does not divide. This is exploration; it earns nothing and proves nothing.
authorship: Original Primer explanations, examples and implementation. No Brilliant lesson text, artwork or question bank is included.

sequences.note: The guided challenges this model once listed are now learning sequences on the shared player, marked by the server.

knowledge.definition: A positive integer d divides N when N = d × q for an integer q, leaving remainder zero.
knowledge.one_digit: Write N = 10 × q + r. When d divides 10, the tens contribute no remainder, so only r matters. This covers 2, 5 and 10.
knowledge.two_digits: Write N = 100 × q + r. Since 100 is a multiple of 4, divisibility by 4 depends on the final two digits.
knowledge.uncertainty: A final 0 alone does not settle divisibility by 4: 40 is divisible by 4, but 50 is not.
knowledge.suffix_rule: When d divides 10ᵏ, the last k digits give the remainder on division by d. Three digits suffice for 8 and 125, and four suffice for 16.
knowledge.place_value_remainders: For each place, multiply the digit by the remainder of its place value. Add those contributions and reduce the sum by the divisor.

game_model.mastery: Exploration only; no XP, streak, assessment pass or mastery write.
game_model.number_representation: Decimal strings evaluated with BigInt; leading zeroes allowed.
